content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm looking to set up a wireless link between a [product_name] controller and remote I/Os (like switches, solenoids, sensors, etc.), since the system needs to be moved frequently and wiring becomes a challenge, especially with a distance of around 50 meters. What equipment should be used on both ends, and what additional accessories are required? Would it be feasible to use wireless connectivity just for digital I/Os? I would greatly appreciate it if anyone could share their experience on this.
Hello, Unfortunately, wireless I/O modules for [product_name] are not available from [company_name]. Best regards, [user_name]

Hello, You could consider hybrid solutions—such as using wireless devices built on EnOcean technology with a KNX/EnOcean gateway and a [product_name] controller equipped with a KNX communication module, along with power supplies and KNX/USB accessories. Another option is wireless I/O actuators paired with the controller, where signals are transmitted from sensors to actuators and then to the controller.
Thank you for your response. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users are seeking wireless solutions to connect remote I/Os with [product_name] controllers, mainly due to the difficulties posed by wiring when the system is mobile and the distances involved. Since dedicated wireless I/O modules are not offered by [company_name], discussion centers around exploring third-party wireless technologies and integration accessories. The conversation reveals a strong demand for user-friendly, reliable wireless options to address flexible connectivity needs in industrial environments—a demand that existing products do not fully meet.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate that [company_name] [product_name] controllers will support wireless I/O connections or supply compatible solutions along with clear guidance on necessary accessories for both analog and digital I/Os. They seek easy-to-implement wireless connectivity options suitable for distances up to 50 meters.
